card.title: The *story*
card.text: On Sunday 29 October 2017 in Canberra, Lebanon beat France 29-18 for their first ever win at a Rugby League World Cup, at their first World Cup since 2000. Travis Robinson scored twice, Anthony Layoun and 19-year-old Adam Doueihi crossed, and Mitchell Moses added a try, four goals and a field goal.

caption:
From the archive: on this day in 2017, the Cedars made history. 🏉

Nine years ago today, Lebanon beat France 29-18 in Canberra for their first ever Rugby League World Cup win. Travis Robinson scored twice, and Mitchell Moses added a try, four goals and a field goal.

This Sunday, 1 November, Lebanon and France meet again at the 2026 World Cup.

Who remembers this one? 🇱🇧

📸 naparazzi (Flickr) / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0 (Adam Doueihi in 2017)
Source: RLWC 2017, Sky Sports, NSWRL
@lebanonrl
#SportsWireLB #FromTheArchive #RugbyLeague

The story: on Sunday 29 October 2017 in Canberra, Lebanon beat France 29-18 for their first ever Rugby League World Cup win, at their first World Cup since 2000; tries by Travis Robinson (2), Anthony Layoun, 19-year-old Adam Doueihi and Mitchell Moses, who also kicked four goals and a field goal.
The match: Rugby League World Cup, Sunday 29 October 2017, Canberra Stadium: France 18, Lebanon 29. Lebanon tries: Robinson 2, Layoun, Doueihi, Moses. Moses: a try, four goals and a field goal.
Then and now: 2017, Lebanon's first World Cup win, against France in Canberra; 2026, Lebanon and France meet again at the World Cup on Sunday 1 November at CommBank Stadium in Sydney.
